raw:
The user wants me to act as a hardware security expert and extract runtime-checkable security invariants for OpenTitan's otp_ctrl module. They've given me SEC_CM annotations from the RTL files, and they want invariants for security-sensitive data paths (keys/seeds/masks/digests/erase/state machines).

The rule types supported:
- wipe_clears: after triggering erase register, target signal must be cleared (or become erase mode value)
- changes_across_runs: randomness signals (masks/entropy) must differ across two independent runs
- reg_core_consistent: same data in reg-side and core-side copies must be consistent

Each invariant needs trigger_regs (register write sequence that triggers the check).

Let me think about otp_ctrl architecture:

OpenTitan OTP controller has:
- Direct Access Interface (DAI) - registers like DIRECT_ACCESS_CMD, DIRECT_ACCESS_ADDRESS, DIRECT_ACCESS_WDATA_0/1, DIRECT_ACCESS_RDATA_0/1
- Secret partitions: TEST_TOKENS, SECRET_MANUFACTURING_PARTITION, SECRET_PROD_PARTITION_0/1/2/3 (in newer versions), each with scrambling
- Scrambling engine: otp_ctrl_scrmbl.sv with FSM (SEC_CM: SCRMBL.FSM.SPARSE), counter redundancy (SCRMBL.CTR.REDUN), local/global escalation (SCRMBL.FSM.LOCAL_ESC, SCRMBL.FSM.GLOBAL_ESC)
- Partition buffers: otp_ctrl_part_buf.sv with access control (SEC_CM: ACCESS.CTRL.MUBI), FSM sparse (PART.FSM.SPARSE), background check (PART.DATA_REG.BKGN_CHK), digest (PART.MEM.DIGEST), scrambling (SECRET.MEM.SCRAMBLE)
- Lifecycle partition with LC transition interface
- Key manager outputs: keymgr_key_o (creator root key, owner intermediate key), flash/OTP seeds
- Digests: HW digest for partitions, consistency digest
- Wipe: lc_escalate_en_i triggers wiping of secret partitions (SECRET_WIPE)

Key registers in otp_ctrl (from otp_ctrl_reg.hjson):
- INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST, ALERT_TEST
- STATUS
- DIRECT_ACCESS_REGWEN, DIRECT_ACCESS_CMD (RD, WR, DIGEST, SEC_WIPE), DIRECT_ACCESS_ADDRESS, DIRECT_ACCESS_WDATA_0, DIRECT_ACCESS_WDATA_1, DIRECT_ACCESS_RDATA_0, DIRECT_ACCESS_RDATA_1
- CHECK_TRIGGER_REGWEN, CHECK_TRIGGER (INTEGRITY, CONSISTENCY)
- CHECK_REGWEN, CHECK_TIMEOUT, INTEGRITY_CHECK_PERIOD, CONSISTENCY_CHECK_PERIOD
- SW_CFG_WINDOW_READ_LOCK (in newer versions)
- Vendor test registers (VENDOR_TEST_READ_LOCK?)

The wipe mechanism: DIRECT_ACCESS_CMD.SEC_WIPE triggers a secure wipe of a secret partition. Also lc_escalate_en_i (life cycle escalation) triggers global wipe of all secret partitions.

Signals in otp_ctrl_core:
- u_core.u_part_bufs[i] - partition buffers
- Secret partitions store data in part_buf arrays: e.g., u_core.u_part_bufs[SecretManufPartIdx].data_buf_q or similar
- Scrambling engine: u_core.u_scrmbl (otp_ctrl_scrmbl) with data_out, key, etc.
